items.text:
Subject: Music Gear Lending Desk — Fall Reservations Now Open

Dear Nadia,

The Department of Music has opened its instrument and audio-gear lending desk in the basement of Hartley Hall, Room B12. I know you've been hauling your keyboard back and forth from your apartment, so this should save you some trouble.

The desk lends keyboards, practice amps, recording mics, and small mixers for a full semester at a time. You need to reserve online through the department portal at least three days before pickup, and staff will not release anything without a student ID. First-time borrowers also pay a $25 refundable deposit, which is returned when the gear comes back on time. Items returned late add $5 per day, and after two weeks the equipment is considered lost.

Desk hours are Monday through Thursday, 1:00 to 6:00 PM. If you want a slot before midterms, book this week — the amps go fast.

Best regards,
Devon Ruiz
Music Student Association

format_metadata.subject: Music Gear Lending Desk — Fall Reservations Now Open

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the email?

options.A: To remind a student about an overdue piece of equipment
options.B: To announce that music classes will move to Hartley Hall
options.C: To describe a new equipment lending service and its rules
options.D: To compare the prices of keyboards at campus shops

questions.explanation: The email introduces the music department's new instrument and audio-gear lending desk and explains how it works, including the reservation process, deposit, late fees, and desk hours. Options A, B, and D describe purposes the email does not have.

questions.stem: According to the email, what must borrowers do before picking up equipment?

options.A: To pay a deposit in cash at the lending desk
options.B: To reserve the item online three days in advance
options.C: To bring a signed form from the department office
options.D: To return the equipment within two weeks

questions.explanation: The email states that borrowers must reserve online through the department portal at least three days before pickup. The deposit is refundable and is not described as a cash payment at the desk, no signed form is mentioned, and the two-week period refers to when a late item is treated as lost.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the practice amps?

options.A: They are in high demand among students.
options.B: They are too heavy to carry to the basement.
options.C: They are available only to first-time borrowers.
options.D: They are loaned for a period of two weeks.

questions.explanation: The writer advises booking this week because 'the amps go fast,' which implies that they are popular and run out quickly. Nothing in the email says they are heavy, restricted to new borrowers, or loaned for only two weeks.

items.text:
NOTICE: Required Wi-Fi Security Certificate Update
Office of Information Technology — Meridian University

Beginning Monday, November 4, all students, faculty, and staff must install the new secure-network certificate (version 4.2) on every personal device used to access campus Wi-Fi. The current certificate is scheduled to expire at 11:59 PM on Sunday, November 3.

The update takes about ten minutes and can be completed through the campus portal. Devices left on the old certificate will be disconnected automatically and will not be able to reach library databases, course portals, or printing services.

- Install the certificate on laptops, tablets, and phones before November 3.
- Connect to the "MU-Secure" network in order to complete the installation.
- Keep the original certificate until the new one is confirmed.
- Visit the Tech Desk in Sawyer Hall, Room 110, for in-person help.

Walk-in assistance is available Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. A $15 service fee is charged for staff-assisted installation on devices brought to the desk; the online method is free of charge.

Questions may be sent to network@meridian.edu.

format_metadata.from: Office of Information Technology, Meridian University
format_metadata.title: Required Wi-Fi Security Certificate Update

questions.stem: According to the notice, what happens to devices that keep using the old certificate?

options.A: They lose access to certain campus services.
options.B: They must be brought to Sawyer Hall.
options.C: They are charged a fifteen-dollar fee.
options.D: They update themselves through the portal.

questions.explanation: The notice says such devices are disconnected automatically and cannot reach library databases, course portals, or printing services. Bringing a device to the Tech Desk is optional, the $15 fee applies only to staff-assisted installation, and no automatic updating is described.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about installing the certificate online?

options.A: It requires a visit to the Tech Desk first.
options.B: It takes longer than the staff-assisted method.
options.C: It avoids the fifteen-dollar service charge.
options.D: It must be finished before November 4.

questions.explanation: The notice states that the $15 fee is charged only for staff-assisted installation and that the online method is free, so users who install it themselves pay nothing. Option D swaps the real deadline of November 3 for the start date of November 4.

questions.stem: What can be inferred about the certificate students currently have?

options.A: It was created by the Tech Desk staff in Sawyer Hall.
options.B: It will stop working on the first weekend of November.
options.C: It must be removed before the new one is installed.
options.D: It works on phones but not on tablet computers.

questions.explanation: The current certificate expires at 11:59 PM on Sunday, November 3, which is the first weekend of November, so it will cease to function then. The notice actually tells users to keep the old certificate until the new one is confirmed, and it never says who created it or that it works on only some devices.
